southern-draw--kudzu.description: The first cigar from Southern Draw, the brand Robert and Sharon Holt founded in 2014, Kudzu is rolled at A.J. Fernandez in Estelí: aged Nicaraguan binder and filler under a twice-fermented Ecuadorian Habano Oscuro wrapper. It opens peppery and creamy, then settles into cedar, chocolate, coffee and dried fruit, with strength building toward the band.

thirds.notes: Strong black pepper with chocolate, cream and malt, plus espresso and cedar in the background.
Raisin and cherry sweetness with orange, chocolate and coffee; leather and a nutty note appear as the cedar fades.
The spice stays present as strength rises and the nuttiness grows; the flavors keep their balance.

southern-draw--firethorn.description: Southern Draw's second line, rolled at A.J. Fernandez, sets a double-fermented Ecuadorian Habano Rosado wrapper over a Mexican San Andrés binder and Nicaraguan filler. At the gentler end of medium, it trades on baking spice, cocoa and roasted pecan, with a cooked, cherry-like fruit sweetness through the middle.

thirds.notes: Cinnamon and baking spice with fruit sweetness, pecan, cocoa powder and red pepper that softens into the finish.
A burnt, cherry-like fruit takes the lead with spice behind, as roasted pecan, chocolate and coffee bean build.
Deeply roasted pecan and burnt fruit with rising spice, a little leather and smoky hardwood.

southern-draw--rose-of-sharon.description: Shipped in 2017, Rose of Sharon is Southern Draw's Connecticut blend: an Ecuadorian sun-grown Connecticut wrapper on a Nicaraguan binder, with Nicaraguan viso and seco and a ligero of Piloto Cubano and Dominican tobacco. Medium and creamy, it offers a honeyed, cereal-like sweetness with nuts, cedar and coffee; a calm, even-tempered smoke.

thirds.notes: Honeyed, cereal-like sweetness with nougat and nuts, early pepper and a sweet citrus note.
Smoother and creamier, with cedar giving way to lighter oak, coffee building and almond on the finish.
Grainy, toasted notes with cedar and oak; some smokes finish on dark, baking-style chocolate.

southern-draw--jacob-s-ladder.description: A double-ligero blend from Southern Draw, made at A.J. Fernandez and released nationwide in 2017: Pennsylvania Broadleaf from Lancaster over an Ecuadorian maduro binder and Nicaraguan filler with ligero from Estelí and Jalapa. Rich rather than harsh, it pairs dark chocolate and espresso with dark fruit, earth and pepper.

thirds.notes: Juicy dark fruit, sweet dark chocolate and espresso, with black pepper over cedar and leather.
Darker and bigger: earth and espresso at the core, a chili-like spice on the retrohale and touches of oak.
Sweetness recedes as dark-roast coffee returns, with strong pepper alongside leather, cedar and chocolate.

southern-draw--cedrus.description: Southern Draw's fifth core blend, introduced in 2018 and named for the Lebanese cedar, wraps an Estelí Habano 2000 binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler in a late-harvest Besuki leaf from Java; it is made at A.J. Fernandez. Cedar runs through it, with pepper, anise and earth, then cocoa and citrus toward the end.

thirds.notes: Sweet cedar and black pepper trade the lead, with leather, earth, espresso and an anise-like note.
Earthier and fuller, as cedar and sweet tobacco alternate over cocoa, baking spice and softened pepper.
Dark chocolate with a citrus edge, leather and earth return, and the smoke turns creamy with a peanut note.

southern-draw--300-hands.description: Introduced in 2018, 300 Hands is named for the many hands a cigar passes through from seed to shelf, and a share of its profits goes to Nicaraguan communities. This maduro version wraps an Indonesian binder in a near-black Estelí leaf, rolled at A.J. Fernandez. Mocha leads, with coffee, pepper, cedar and a faint orange sweetness.

thirds.notes: Chocolate-led mocha with white and black pepper, cedar, a hint of walnut and a soft orange sweetness.
The coffee side of the mocha grows while the chocolate fades; pepper rises and wood comes forward.
Coffee dominates with pepper as the main counterpoint, plus cocoa, wood, light leather and a citrus note.

southern-draw--300-manos.description: The Habano-wrapped counterpart to 300 Hands, launched by Southern Draw at the 2018 trade show and made at A.J. Fernandez, with filler from Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic. A steady medium throughout, it leans sweet and spiced: cocoa, caramel, baking spice and cedar, with pepper and leather gathering at the end.

thirds.notes: Cocoa and baking spice with creaminess, a cashew-like nuttiness and a dry, grassy edge; white pepper on the retrohale.
Caramel, cinnamon and cedar with chocolate and creamy coffee, mixed fruit and a toffee-like sweetness.
Peppercorn returns and grows, leather moves to the front and the texture turns creamy, with buttery cocoa.
